authorization_basis: Current repository user_fixed_constraints require all 19 intended existing non-primary roles to remain active and explicitly authorize optimizer re-enable-only reconciliation after readback/cause check when an intended enabled_desired role is physically stopped.

observations: Control10 recorded 19/19 enabled after repair at 17:39:36+09:00.
A later exact live inventory again found 13/19.
Five of the six newly disabled roles were also disabled in the prior drift set; cross_field remained enabled while integrator newly joined the disabled set.
For every newly disabled task, platform updated_at followed last_run by roughly one minute.
Re-enable-only updates on the same six task ids restored each task with is_enabled=true readback.
Current repository controls still require enabled_desired=true and Phase 1 remains incomplete.
cause_assessment.inference: The recurrence is strongly correlated with a post-invocation/scheduler-lifecycle boundary rather than a static role-id or capacity configuration. The responsible actor remains unproven; do not label it worker self-disable or platform auto-disable without direct evidence.
cause_assessment.method_adjustment: Preserve exact last_run and updated_at boundaries on every recurrence and correlate them with the role-local terminal receipt before any semantic reassignment. If the receipt proves global_completion=false with a nonempty Phase-1 continuation yet the task still disables, classify platform_lifecycle_disable_after_noncompletion. If the receipt itself requested or asserted scheduler completion, repair that role's repository terminal/continuation method with a revision increment, then re-enable the same task. Until one branch is proven, do not churn unrelated role assignments.
cause_assessment.required_followup: After the next scheduled invocations of the repaired roles, inspect live enabled state first. On recurrence, preserve the exact pre-repair platform metadata and fetch the corresponding current-control terminal receipt before re-enable. Continue re-enable-only immediately after evidence capture so the 19-role pool is not reduced.

phase1_effect.reason_root_still_open: The pool is repaired to 19/19, but a third drift recurrence makes scheduler persistence a repeated blocker. Current control10/26/33 execution evidence, Work-dependency-elimination matrix, zero-residual/zero-quota/cost controls, rate-limit resume and aggregate acceptance gates remain incomplete.

exact_next_action: Keep all 19 intended roles active. At the next invocation inspect live physical state before semantic optimization. If any repaired role is disabled, capture exact last_run/updated_at and current-control terminal receipt before re-enable-only reconciliation; use that evidence to distinguish a platform lifecycle disable from a role terminal-contract defect and repair only the proven cause. rollback: Supersede only with newer exact platform and receipt evidence. Never disable a managed role, lower the 19-role denominator, restore historical handoff acceptance, weaken user-fixed constraints, or modify primary O/protected recovery.
